fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are admitted to MQTT v5 parsing; the 8-byte PoC (30 06 00 01 61 02 01 00) is a PUBLISH packet whose remaining-length field consumes the whole input, so the parsed datagram ends exactly at the heap-buffer end.
dgram.len becomes 8 == input size, so end = dgram.buf + dgram.len is one byte past the heap allocation; any read at that address is a heap-buffer-overflow.
For the PUBLISH packet props_start = 6 and props_size = 2 are taken from the input (property length varint 0x02, properties 0x01 0x00); the properties section ends exactly at dgram.len.

Property iteration starts with ofs = 0 and each call's return value becomes the next ofs; the first BYTE property (id 0x01, value 0x00) returns new_pos = 2, so the loop re-enters mg_mqtt_next_prop with ofs = 2.
The read pointer is computed from attacker-controlled props_start and ofs; on the second call props_start(6) + ofs(2) == dgram.len(8), so i == end.
end delimits the valid datagram region; the guard at line 211 mis-compares ofs (not props_start + ofs) against dgram.len, so it cannot reject the out-of-range pointer.

The 1-byte read of the property identifier executes unconditionally BEFORE the bounds check on line 211; the safety condition that should hold first is msg->props_start + ofs < msg->dgram.len (i < end).
First call parses the BYTE property (id byte + value byte) and returns new_pos = 2; the loop passes ofs = 2 into the next call, placing i exactly at end.

Second call with ofs = 2: i == end == dgram.buf + dgram.len, one byte past the 8-byte heap buffer; the dereference i[0] performs the heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 (ASan: src/mqtt.c in mg_mqtt_next_prop, called from fuzz.c:68).
